0009 · Visualizer from the master tap, on its own screen

Status · Accepted · 2026-11-06

Context

The owner asked for customisable real-time visualizers, kept independent of the mixing interface, that can be cast or extended to external displays and run full screen at shows.

Decision

  • The engine publishes a visual tap: the newest 8192 mono master samples, written after the latency-compensation delay so pictures match the speakers. Any thread can read it with sbe_engine_read_visual. Reading never blocks the audio thread.
  • A VisualizerFeed turns the tap into frames: a 2048-point FFT into 32 log bands (fast attack, slow release), a 512-sample scope, the level, and the beat phase of the deck on air. It runs only while a visualizer is on screen.
  • Four styles share one frame: Spectrum, Radial, Scope and Pulse (the brand element, driven by the music). Three palettes; spectral uses the waveform band colours.
  • Second screen by platform:
    • iOS and iPadOS: an external display or AirPlay screen gets its own non-interactive scene with the visualizer (a setting can turn it off). The phone keeps the decks.
    • macOS: the visualizer is a separate window that can move to any display and go full screen.
    • Android (later): the Presentation API on a secondary display.
  • On the device itself, a full-screen stage with auto-hiding controls.

Consequences

  • The visualizer cannot affect audio: it only reads a copy of the master.
  • Mirroring is replaced on iOS when the setting is on, which is what a performer wants. Turning it off restores normal mirroring.

Source: docs/decisions/0009-visualizer-and-second-screen.md
